preamble: The shift from the palatal nasal [ɲ] to the alveolar nasal [n] is known as depalatalization. This process often occurs in word-final positions or as part of a general simplification of the consonant system, moving from a more marked palatal sound to a more common alveolar one.

examples.note: In many dialects, Spanish word-final [ɲ] (though rare and often appearing in loans or as a result of specific processes) is realized as or reduced to the alveolar [n].
Historical developments in Romanian saw several palatalized nasals depalatalizing to alveolar nasals.

examples.to: Proto-Southern Jê *nĩ; Kaingang nĩ, Laklãnõ nẽ
Proto-Southern Jê *nĩjã; Kaingang nĩjẽ, Laklãnõ nẽjã
Proto-Southern Jê *nũr; Kaingang nũr, Laklãnõ nũl
Proto-Southern Jê *nũnã; Kaingang nũnẽ, Laklãnõ nũnã
examples.note: Proto-Jê */j/ had the nasal allophone *ñ before nasal vowels; Proto-Southern Jê turned onset *ñ into *n, merging it with *n, while oral *j stayed *j. Forms in Nikulin's Macro-Jê alphabet: ñ = [ɲ], j = [j ~ ʒ], c = [tʃ ~ tɕ ~ ts ~ c], ĵ = [dʒ ~ ɟ], ə̂ = [ɘ ~ ɤ], y = [ɨ ~ ɯ], ê/ô = close-mid [e]/[o], ṭʰ = aspirated alveolar stop, mb/nd = post-oralized nasals; a final ’ marks a coda without echo vowel, X // Y gives phrase-medial // prepausal allomorphs.

examples.to: Kĩsêdjê mben; Parkatêjê, Canela, Gavião-Pyhcopji pen

examples.note: Coda *ñ became n independently in Proto-Timbíra and in Kĩsêdjê; Mẽbêngôkre and Apinajé keep ñ, and Tapayúna has j instead. Forms in Nikulin's Macro-Jê alphabet: ñ = [ɲ], j = [j ~ ʒ], c = [tʃ ~ tɕ ~ ts ~ c], ĵ = [dʒ ~ ɟ], ə̂ = [ɘ ~ ɤ], y = [ɨ ~ ɯ], ê/ô = close-mid [e]/[o], ṭʰ = aspirated alveolar stop, mb/nd = post-oralized nasals; a final ’ marks a coda without echo vowel, X // Y gives phrase-medial // prepausal allomorphs.
